correctness.rationale: For distinct Euclidean vertices strict negative type makes the normalized small-scale magnitude weighting converge to the unique distance-energy maximizer on total mass one. Rotational symmetry reduces its Euler–Lagrange equations to two orbit masses u=(S−C)/(nΔ), v=(rS−C)/(nΔ), with Δ=(1+r)S−2C<0 by strict negative type of the signed orbit contrast. C_n(r) has C′(0)=0, C″(r)>0 and C(0)=n<S<C(1)=2csc(π/(2n)), so the zero u-threshold r_n is unique; C(cosπ/n)<S follows from the midpoint triangle inequality. For r>cosπ/n all 2n points are uniquely exposed by their radial directions. Taylor expansion at r=1 with C″=O(n log n) gives r_n=1−π²/(4n²)+O(log n/n⁴). Independent computations verified thresholds/negative inner masses/convex position at n=4,5,8,12 and convergence n²(1−r_n)→π²/4 up to n=160, without claiming finite checks prove the asymptotic.
residual_risks: Finite diagnostics alone cannot prove the universal aspects; the cited arguments supply those steps.
